description: The bar chart illustrates the number of hateful communication datasets published annually from 2012 to 2022, categorized by the location of the researchers who created them, as presented in the paper “The Unseen Targets of Hate — A Systematic Review of Hateful Communication Datasets.” The vertical axis, labeled “Number of datasets,” is plotted on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ (1) to 10² (100), with major gridlines at 1, 10, and 100. The horizontal axis represents the year, spanning from 2012 to 2022. Each year features a grouped set of vertical bars, each corresponding to a researcher location: “Other” (blue), “UK” (red), “USA” (orange), “IT” (purple), “IN” (green), and “DE” (brown), as indicated in the legend titled “Researcher Location.” In early years (2012–2015), datasets are sparse, with only a few entries, mostly from “USA” and “Other.” From 2016 onward, dataset production increases significantly, with “Other” consistently contributing the highest number of datasets each year, peaking at over 100 in 2021. “USA” and “IN” also show strong growth, with “USA” reaching approximately 30–40 datasets in 2020–2021 and “IN” exceeding 20 in 2021. “UK,” “IT,” and “DE” contribute fewer datasets overall, with “UK” and “DE” showing modest increases over time and “IT” fluctuating, notably dropping to near zero in 2022. The chart visually emphasizes the dominance of “Other” locations in dataset creation, particularly in later years, while also highlighting the growing global participation in hate speech dataset development.
